question: Should upgrades with a pre-existing SQLite database and an unreceipted legacy `runs.json` fail closed and require operator recovery, or must this PR provide a safe explicit recovery/import action before merge?
rationale: The source cannot establish whether an unreceipted JSON file is stale or the only remaining legitimate registry, so choosing between resurrection prevention and preserving recoverable runs is an upgrade-policy decision.

options.title: Add explicit recovery before merge
options.body: Preserve the fail-closed default but provide a doctor-guided, auditable action that lets operators inspect and intentionally import or discard the ambiguous source.

options.title: Accept fail-closed operator recovery
options.body: Land the current policy with clear release-note recovery instructions and maintainer ownership of the possibility that legitimate runs become temporarily invisible.

recommendation.title: Add explicit recovery before merge
recommendation.body: Preserve the fail-closed default but provide a doctor-guided, auditable action that lets operators inspect and intentionally import or discard the ambiguous source.

likelyOwner.reason: The current registry persistence and migration boundary appears to originate from their merged SQLite registry work.
